cases.purpose: A clock-setting request (date -s STRING / date MMDDhhmm[[CC]YY][.ss]) sets CLOCK_REALTIME to the requested instant and prints it; recorded against a mock without changing the real clock
cases.oracle: GNU date (coreutils) in the guest, run through the same seccomp-notify mock (clock_settime/settimeofday answered with success and recorded), as the independent expectation of the setter request
cases.comparison: Printed new time and the recorded clock-set request (seconds, nanoseconds, CLOCK_REALTIME) for both forms, GNU versus candidate; the real clock is untouched.
cases.script:
[[ $UID == 2000 && $EUID == 2000 && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || exit 125
IFS= read -r marker </etc/bashos-parity-vm || exit 125
IFS= read -r vendor </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor || exit 125
[[ $vendor == QEMU && $marker =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$ ]] || exit 125
[[ $(type -t date) == builtin ]] || exit 125
SEQ=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-sequence.py
RULES="--notify clock_settime --log-args clock_settime=0 --log-mem clock_settime=1:16 --notify settimeofday --log-mem settimeofday=0:16 --reply clock_settime=0 --reply settimeofday=0"
# trial LABEL COMMAND : run COMMAND in a filtered shell with clock setters answered by a mock success
trial() {
  local label=$1 cmd=$2 T=$HOME/$1
  /usr/bin/python3 "$SEQ" $RULES --log "$T.log" -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$cmd" scn >"$T.out" 2>"$T.err"
  local rc=$?
  /usr/bin/python3 -I - "$T" "$label" "$rc" <<'PY'
import json, os, struct, sys
t, label, rc = sys.argv[1:]
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(t + ".log")] if os.path.exists(t + ".log") else []
reqs = []
for r in rows:
    key = "memory1" if r["syscall"] == "clock_settime" else "memory0"
    raw = bytes.fromhex(r[key]["hex"])
    sec, sub = struct.unpack("<qq", raw)
    reqs.append((sec, sub if r["syscall"] == "clock_settime" else sub * 1000, r["syscall"] == "settimeofday" or r["arg0"] == 0))
out = open(t + ".out").read().rstrip("\n")
err = open(t + ".err").read()
first = "none" if not reqs else "sec=%d nsec=%d realtime=%d" % reqs[0]
print("%s: rc=%s out=[%s] requests=%d first: %s unknown-arg=%d" % (label, rc, out, len(reqs), first, "unknown arg" in err))
PY
}
trial gnu-s "/usr/bin/date -u -s '2000-01-01 00:00:00'"
trial cand-s "date -u -s '2000-01-01 00:00:00'"
trial gnu-mmdd "/usr/bin/date -u 010100002000"
trial cand-mmdd "date -u 010100002000"
now=$(/usr/bin/date +%s); echo "real-clock-unchanged=$(( now > 1900000000 || now < 1000000000 ? 0 : 1 ))"
cases.stdout:
gnu-s: rc=0 out=[Sat Jan  1 00:00:00 UTC 2000] requests=1 first: sec=946684800 nsec=0 realtime=1 unknown-arg=0
cand-s: rc=0 out=[Sat Jan  1 00:00:00 UTC 2000] requests=1 first: sec=946684800 nsec=0 realtime=1 unknown-arg=0
gnu-mmdd: rc=0 out=[Sat Jan  1 00:00:00 UTC 2000] requests=1 first: sec=946684800 nsec=0 realtime=1 unknown-arg=0
cand-mmdd: rc=0 out=[Sat Jan  1 00:00:00 UTC 2000] requests=1 first: sec=946684800 nsec=0 realtime=1 unknown-arg=0
real-clock-unchanged=1

cases.purpose: Setter syntax the candidate does not support (date -s @0, date 010100002000) is rejected with failure and a diagnostic, and no clock mutation is requested
cases.oracle: The candidate's documented option set (-u -R -I --rfc-3339 -d +FORMAT) as the contract: anything else is an unknown argument; the seccomp-notify mock records no clock_settime/settimeofday call
cases.comparison: Status, diagnostic and absence of any recorded setter call for two unsupported forms.
